name: dsh-vllm-bridge
description: Runs the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) entirely on your vLLM-Copilot registry: your models, your servers, your token totals, no DeepSeek account.
author: Dieter Schwarzmann <info@systemwissenschaften.de>

dsh-bridge-whale.description: DSH whale, spouting: the harness is running.

dsh-bridge-whale-off.description: DSH whale at rest: the harness is stopped.

dsh-bridge.dshVersion.markdownDescription: Run a specific `@deepseek-ai/dsh` version instead of the one this bridge was certified against. Accepts `latest` or an exact version like `0.2.0-rc.2`; anything else is ignored. Leave empty unless you are testing a new release: dsh's semver is decorative and an uncertified version can change its config rows under us.

dsh-bridge.defaultModelId.description: Registry model id the harness should use by default. Empty uses the first configured model.

dsh-bridge.titleModel.description: Registry model id for session-title calls. Empty uses the default model.

dsh-bridge.titleMaxTokens.description: Output cap for session-title calls. 0 leaves it to the model's own limit.

dsh-bridge.compactionModel.description: Registry model id for context-compaction calls. Empty uses the default model.

dsh-bridge.compactionMaxTokens.description: Output cap for context-compaction calls. 0 leaves it to the model's own limit.

dsh-bridge.openIn.markdownDescription: Where the harness UI opens. `panel` (default) docks a **chromeless webview** fed by the extension's embed proxy — no address bar, a stable URL that survives harness restarts, and no token in browser history. `appWindow` opens the same stable URL in a bar-less Edge/Chrome `--app` window. `embedded` uses the built-in browser view (its toolbar cannot be hidden; VS Code exposes no setting for it). `external` always uses the system browser. Every embedded door falls back to the next when unavailable.

dsh-bridge.embedPort.description: Loopback port the embed proxy listens on for the panel and app-window doors. A fixed port gives the chromeless UI one URL that survives every harness restart; if another window holds it, the proxy falls back to an ephemeral port on its own. 0 asks Windows for any free port.

dsh-bridge.drainTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a restart waits for in-flight harness requests to finish before stopping the harness anyway. 0 restarts immediately and cuts live requests.

dsh-bridge.ingestIntervalSeconds.description: How often completed harness requests are folded into the vLLM-Copilot usage ledger.

dsh-bridge.logLevel.markdownDescription: Developer verbosity intent for the **DeepSeek Harness Bridge** log channel. The bridge always emits its Debug-tier lines — every harness stdout/stderr mirror (boot chatter otherwise dropped) and every MCP JSON-RPC method and tool call — but VS Code gates them by the channel's own log level. Setting this to `debug`/`trace` reveals the channel and points at its gear › **Set Log Level…** picker, which persists. Never restarts the harness.

dsh-bridge.keyboardBridge.description: Forward keyboard shortcuts that the harness page does not consume (F1, Ctrl+Shift+P, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+Shift+E/F, Ctrl+,, Ctrl+W) to VS Code while focus is inside a harness view. The harness keeps any shortcut it handles itself.

scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile && npm run test:e2e:compile && node scripts/e2e-stand-in.mjs && node -e "require('node:fs').mkdirSync('temp/e2e-workspace',{recursive:true})" && node node_modules/@vscode/test-cli/out/bin.mjs
scripts.bridge:check: tsc -p tsconfig.json && node scripts/stage-core.mjs && node scripts/step3-bridge-check.mjs
